claim: Voltage-gated potassium (KV) channels are important regulators of cellular excitability and control action potential repolarization in the heart and brain.
source: Voltage-gated potassium (KV) channels are important regulators of cellular excitability and control action potential repolarization in the heart and brain.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about KV channels.

claim: KV channel mutations lead to disordered cellular excitability.
source: KV channel mutations lead to disordered cellular excitability.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the consequences of KV channel mutations.

claim: Loss-of-function mutations in KV channels result in membrane hyperexcitability, a characteristic of epilepsy and cardiac arrhythmias.
source: Loss-of-function mutations, for example, result in membrane hyperexcitability, a characteristic of epilepsy and cardiac arrhythmias.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the pathophysiological consequences of loss-of-function KV channel mutations.

claim: Polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) and PUFA analogues comprise a class of KV channel activators with potential applications in the treatment of arrhythmogenic disorders such as long QT syndrome (LQTS).
source: Polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) and PUFA analogues comprise a class of KV channel activators with potential applications in the treatment of arrhythmogenic disorders such as long QT syndrome (LQTS).
evidence: This is a statement about the potential therapeutic application of PUFAs, based on their known activating effects.

claim: LQTS is caused by a loss-of-function of the cardiac IKs channel.
source: LQTS is caused by a loss-of-function of the cardiac IKs channel – a tetrameric potassium channel complex formed by KV7.1 and associated KCNE1 protein subunits.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the molecular basis of LQTS.

claim: The cardiac IKs channel is a tetrameric potassium channel complex formed by KV7.1 and associated KCNE1 protein subunits.
source: LQTS is caused by a loss-of-function of the cardiac IKs channel – a tetrameric potassium channel complex formed by KV7.1 and associated KCNE1 protein subunits.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the molecular composition of the IKs channel.

claim: A set of aromatic PUFA analogues produce robust activation of the cardiac IKs channel.
source: We have discovered a set of aromatic PUFA analogues that produce robust activation of the cardiac IKs channel
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: A unique feature of aromatic PUFA analogues is an aromatic, tyrosine head group.
source: a unique feature of these PUFA analogues is an aromatic, tyrosine head group.
evidence: This is a descriptive statement about the chemical structure of the compounds studied.

claim: Tyrosine PUFA analogues do not activate the IKs channel through cation–pi interactions.
source: We found that tyrosine PUFA analogues do not activate the IKs channel through cation–pi interactions
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data comparing tyrosine and phenylalanine PUFA analogues.

claim: Tyrosine PUFA analogues activate the IKs channel through a combination of hydrogen bonding and ionic interactions.
source: but instead do so through a combination of hydrogen bonding and ionic interactions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data using modified aromatic head groups.

claim: The delayed rectifier potassium channel (IKs) underlies a critical repolarizing current that determines the timing of the ventricular action potential.
source: The delayed rectifier potassium channel (IKs) underlies a critical repolarizing current that determines the timing of the ventricular action potential (Nerbonne and Kass, 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The cardiac IKs current is mediated by the association of the voltage-gated K+ channel KV7.1 α-subunit with the KCNE1 β-subunit.
source: The cardiac IKs current is mediated by the association of the voltage-gated K+ channel KV7.1 α-subunit with the KCNE1 β-subunit (Abramochkin et al., 2018; Wang et al., 1998; Barhanin et al., 1996).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The KV7.1 α-subunit consists of six transmembrane spanning segments, denoted S1–S6 where S1–S4 form the voltage-sensing domain (VSD) and S5–S6 form the pore domain (PD).
source: The KV7.1 α-subunit consists of six transmembrane spanning segments, denoted S1–S6 where S1–S4 form the voltage-sensing domain (VSD) and S5–S6 form the pore domain (PD) (Sun and MacKinnon, 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the structure of KV7.1, supported by a citation.

claim: The S4 segment contains several positively charged arginine residues that allow S4 to move outward, toward the extracellular side of the membrane, when the membrane becomes depolarized.
source: The S4 segment contains several positively charged arginine residues that allow S4 to move outward, toward the extracellular side of the membrane, when the membrane becomes depolarized (Broomand et al., 2003).
evidence: This is established knowledge about voltage sensor function, supported by a citation.

claim: The outward movement of the S4 is transformed into pore opening as a result of conformational changes in the S4–S5 linker of KV7.1.
source: This outward movement of the S4 is transformed into pore opening as a result of conformational changes in the S4–S5 linker of KV7.1 (Kalstrup and Blunck, 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the coupling mechanism, supported by a citation.

claim: Co-expression of KCNE1 with KV7.1 imparts a more depolarized voltage dependence of activation, slower activation kinetics, and increased single-channel conductance compared to KV7.1 alone.
source: Co-expression of KCNE1 with KV7.1 imparts a more depolarized voltage dependence of activation, slower activation kinetics, and increased single-channel conductance compared to KV7.1 alone (Sun et al., 2012; Yang and Sigworth, 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the effects of KCNE1 on KV7.1, supported by citations.

claim: Loss-of-function mutations in the cardiac IKs channel can lead to long QT syndrome (LQTS), which predisposes individuals to ventricular fibrillation and sudden cardiac death.
source: Loss-of-function mutations in the cardiac IKs channel can lead to an arrhythmogenic disorder known as long QT syndrome (LQTS), which predisposes individuals to ventricular fibrillation and sudden cardiac death (Fernández-Falgueras et al., 2017; Roden, 2008; Watanabe et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the clinical consequences of IKs channel mutations, supported by citations.

claim: Current treatments for LQTS include pharmacological intervention with β-blockers or surgical implantation of a cardioverter defibrillator.
source: Current treatments for LQTS include pharmacological intervention with β-blockers or surgical implantation of a cardioverter defibrillator (Waddell-Smith and Skinner, 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge about LQTS treatment, supported by a citation.

claim: Limitations of current LQTS treatments generate a need for novel therapeutic interventions.
source: However, limitations of these treatments generate a need for novel therapeutic interventions to treat LQTS.
evidence: This is a statement about the clinical need for new therapies, based on known limitations of current treatments.

claim: Polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) are amphipathic molecules composed of a charged hydrophilic head group and a long, polyunsaturated hydrophobic tail group.
source: Polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) are amphipathic molecules composed of a charged hydrophilic head group and a long, polyunsaturated hydrophobic tail group (Jump, 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge about PUFA structure, supported by a citation.

claim: PUFAs form a group of IKs channel activators that interact with the channel VSD, thus influencing the voltage dependence of IKs channel activation.
source: It is well documented that PUFAs form a group of IKs channel activators that interact with the channel VSD, thus influencing the voltage dependence of IKs channel activation (Moreno et al., 2015; Moreno et al., 2012; Elinder and Liin, 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge about PUFA effects on IKs channels, supported by citations.

claim: The ability of PUFAs to activate the IKs channel makes them great candidates for potential LQTS therapeutics.
source: The ability of PUFAs to activate the IKs channel makes them great candidates for potential LQTS therapeutics.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the therapeutic potential of PUFAs based on their known effects.

claim: PUFAs promote IKs channel activation through an electrostatic interaction between the negative charge of the hydrophilic PUFA head and positively charged arginine residues in the S4 segment of the IKs channel.
source: PUFAs promote IKs channel activation through an electrostatic interaction between the negative charge of the hydrophilic PUFA head and positively charged arginine residues in the S4 segment of the IKs channel (Elinder and Liin, 2017; Börjesson and Elinder, 2011; Larsson et al., 2020; Börjesson et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mechanism of PUFA action, supported by citations.

claim: Electrostatic activation of the IKs channel by PUFAs is seen as a leftward shift in the voltage dependence of IKs channel activation that leads to increases in IKs current.
source: This electrostatic activation of the IKs channel is seen as a leftward shift in the voltage dependence of IKs channel activation that leads to increases in IKs current.
evidence: This is established knowledge about how PUFA effects manifest functionally.

claim: PUFAs increase IKs current through two independent effects: one on S4 and one on the PD through an electrostatic interaction with a positively charged lysine residue located in S6 (K326).
source: Recently, it has been reported that PUFAs increase IKs current through two independent effects: one on S4 (as described above) and one on the PD through an electrostatic interaction with a positively charged lysine residue located in S6 (K326) (Yazdi et al., 2021; Liin et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the dual mechanism of PUFA action, supported by citations.

claim: The electrostatic interaction with K326 mediates an increase in the maximal conductance (Gmax) of the IKs channel.
source: This electrostatic interaction with the K326 mediates an increase in the maximal conductance (Gmax) of the IKs channel (Yazdi et al., 2021; Liin et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the functional consequence of PUFA interaction with K326, supported by citations.

claim: The lipoelectric hypothesis describes the mechanism through which the negatively charged PUFA head group interacts with positive charges of S4 and S6.
source: The mechanism through which the negatively charged PUFA head group interacts with positive charges of S4 and S6 is called the lipoelectric hypothesis where the polyunsaturated tail of PUFAs and PUFA analogues incorporates into the cell membrane via hydrophobic interactions and electrostatically attracts the outermost gating charges of S4 as well as positively charged K326 in the S6 segment (Börjesson et al., 2008; Yazdi et al., 2021; Bohannon et al., 2019; Bohannon et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the lipoelectric mechanism, supported by citations.

claim: PUFA analogues that have the most robust effects on increasing IKs current are those that have a low pKa value and thus possess a negatively charged head group at physiological pH.
source: PUFA analogues that have the most robust effects on increasing IKs current are those that have a low pKa value and thus possess a negatively charged head group at physiological pH (Bohannon et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge about structure-activity relationships of PUFA analogues, supported by a citation.

claim: PUFAs with glycine or taurine head groups that possess either a carboxyl or sulfonyl head group are examples of PUFA analogues with robust effects on IKs current.
source: Examples include PUFAs with glycine or taurine head groups that possess either a carboxyl or sulfonyl head group, respectively (Bohannon et al., 2020; Liin et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge about specific PUFA analogues, supported by citations.

claim: N-(α-linolenoyl) tyrosine (NALT) has robust effects on IKs current.
source: We have observed that another PUFA analogue, N-(α-linolenoyl) tyrosine (NALT), has robust effects on IKs current.
evidence: This is a finding of the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: NALT is unique in that it possesses a large aromatic tyrosine head group rather than a carboxyl or sulfonyl group present in most of the PUFAs and PUFA analogues that have been characterized.
source: NALT is unique in that it possesses a large aromatic tyrosine head group rather than a carboxyl or sulfonyl group present in most of the PUFAs and PUFA analogues that we have characterized.
evidence: This is a descriptive statement about the chemical structure of NALT.

claim: The presence of highly electronegative groups improves the activating effects of phenylalanine PUFAs on the IKs channel.
source: These data suggest that the presence of highly electronegative groups improve the activating effects of phenylalanine PUFAs on the IKs channel.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data with fluorinated and brominated phenylalanine PUFAs.

claim: Highly electronegative groups on phenylalanine PUFAs do not completely recapitulate the effects of tyrosine PUFAs on the shift in V0.5 of the IKs channel.
source: However, they do not completely recapitulate the effects of tyrosine PUFAs on the shift in V0.5 of the IKs channel.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data comparing fluorinated/brominated phenylalanine PUFAs to tyrosine PUFAs.

claim: 3F-NALT has a fluorine atom adjacent to the tyrosine hydroxyl group that reduces the pKa of the distal hydroxyl group and increases the hydrogen bonding ability.
source: We applied the modified aromatic PUFA analogue N-(α-linolenoyl)–3-fluoro-L-tyrosine (3F-NALT), which has a fluorine atom adjacent to the tyrosine hydroxyl group (Figure 4A). The addition of the fluorine atom reduces the pKa of the distal hydroxyl group and increases the hydrogen bonding ability of said group in 3F-NALT as compared to NALT.
evidence: This is a statement about the chemical properties of 3F-NALT based on known effects of fluorine substitution.

claim: 3F-NALT and NALT have similar maximum effects on I/I0 (3F-NALT: 5.0 ± 1.0; NALT: 5.14 ± 1.2 at 20 μM; p=0.7257).
source: Overall, the maximum effects on I/I0 are similar for 3F-NALT and NALT (3F-NALT: 5.0 ± 1.0; NALT: 5.14 ± 1.2 at 20 μM; p=0.7257, ns; Figure 4B–D).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from experimental data shown in Figure 4B-D.

claim: 3F-NALT induces a significantly greater maximum shift in the V0.5 (ΔV0.5 = –69.3 ± 1.4 at 20 μM) compared to NALT (–56.1 ± 3.6 at 20 μM) (p=0.0298).
source: Notably, 3F-NALT induces a significantly greater maximum shift in the V0.5 (ΔV0.5 = –69.3 ± 1.4 at 20 μM) compared to NALT (–56.1 ± 3.6 AT 20 μM) (p=0.0298*; Figure 4E and F)
evidence: This is a quantitative result from experimental data shown in Figure 4E and F.

claim: The effects of 3F-NALT and NALT on Gmax are not significantly different (3F-NALT: 1.3 ± 0.3; NALT: 1.4 ± 0.3 at 20 μM; p=0.7324).
source: while the effects on Gmax are not significantly different between 3F-NALT and NALT (3F-NALT: 1.3 ± 0.3; NALT: 1.4 ± 0.3 at 20 μM; p=0.7324, ns; Figure 4G and H).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from experimental data shown in Figure 4G and H.

claim: Increasing the hydrogen bonding capacity of the –OH group increases the maximum shift in IKs channel voltage dependence.
source: These data demonstrate that increasing the hydrogen bonding capacity of the –OH group increases the maximum shift in IKs channel voltage dependence.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data comparing 3F-NALT to NALT.

claim: Hydrogen bonding is an important mechanism for IKs activation and preferentially influences the effects on the voltage dependence of IKs activation.
source: This implicates hydrogen bonding as an important mechanism for IKs activation and preferentially influences the effects on the voltage dependence of IKs activation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data showing that enhanced hydrogen bonding increases voltage shift but not Gmax.

claim: R231 has been previously shown to be important for the V0.5 shifting effect of non-aromatic PUFAs.
source: The residue R231, located in the voltage sensor (S4) (Figure 5A), has been previously shown to be important for the V0.5 shifting effect of non-aromatic PUFAs (Liin et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the role of R231, supported by a citation.

claim: The mutation Q234R is necessary to preserve the voltage dependence of activation in IKs channels with the R231Q mutation.
source: The additional mutation Q234R is necessary to preserve the voltage dependence of activation in IKs channels with the R231Q mutation (Liin et al., 2018; Panaghie and Abbott, 2007; Wu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the functional consequences of the R231Q mutation, supported by citations.

claim: The V0.5 shifting effect of Lin-tyr was significantly decreased from ΔV0.5 = –74.4 mV ± 4.1 at 20 μM in the wild-type IKs channel to ΔV0.5 = –36.5 mV ± 7.3 at 20 μM with the R231Q+Q234R mutation (p < 0.0001).
source: The V0.5 shifting effect of Lin-tyr was significantly decreased from ΔV0.5 = –74.4 mV ± 4.1 at 20 μM in the wild-type (WT) IKs channel toΔV0.5 = –36.5 mV ± 7.3 at 20 μM with the R231Q+Q234R mutation (****p < 0.0001; Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from experimental data shown in Figure 5B and C.

claim: R231 contributes to more than half of the voltage dependence shifting effect of Lin-tyr.
source: This reduction indicates that R231 contributes to more than half of the voltage dependence shifting effect of Lin-tyr.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the quantitative reduction in voltage shift observed with the R231Q+Q234R mutation.

claim: The remaining shift in voltage dependence with the R231Q+Q234R mutation is most likely due to PUFA head group interactions with other nearby S4 charges such as R228 and Q234R.
source: The remaining shift is most likely due to PUFA head group interactions with other nearby S4 charges such as R228 and Q234R.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the mechanism of the residual voltage shift.

claim: K326 has been previously shown to be important for the Gmax increasing effect of non-aromatic PUFAs.
source: The residue K326, located near the pore, has been previously shown to be important for the Gmax increasing effect of non-aromatic PUFAs (Liin et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the role of K326, supported by a citation.

claim: The Gmax increasing effect of 3,4,5F NAL-phe was significantly decreased from 2.4 ± 0.4 at 20 μM in the WT IKs channel to 1.22 ± 0.2 at 20 μM with the K326C mutation (p=0.0287).
source: The Gmax increasing effect of 3,4,5F NAL-phe was significantly decreased from 2.4 ± 0.4 at 20 μM in the WT IKs channel to 1.22 ± 0.2 at 20 μM (*p=0.0287; Figure 5E and F).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from experimental data shown in Figure 5E and F.

claim: K326 is necessary for 3,4,5F NAL-phe's Gmax increasing effect.
source: This reduction indicates that K326 is necessary for 3,4,5F NAL-phe's Gmax increasing effect.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the reduction in Gmax effect observed with the K326C mutation.

claim: The mutation R231Q+Q234R significantly decreases the V0.5 shift effect of Lin-tyr but does not change the Gmax increasing effect.
source: The mutation R231Q+Q234R significantly decreases the V0.5 shift effect from ΔV0.5 = –74.4 mV ± 4.1 at 20 μM in the WT IKs channel to ΔV0.5 = –36.5 mV ± 7.3 at 20 μM in the mutation (****p < 0.0001), as mentioned above, but does not change Gmax increasing effect of Lin-tyr (Figure 5G and H).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from experimental data shown in Figure 5G and H.

claim: The mutation K326C significantly decreases the Gmax effect of Lin-tyr from Gmax = 2.04 ± 0.59 at 20 μM in the WT IKs channel to Gmax = 1.08 ± 0.15 at 20 μM in the mutation (p=0.0015) but does not change the V0.5 shift effect.
source: Similarly, the mutation K326C significantly decreases the Gmax effect of Lin-tyr from Gmax = 2.04 ± 0.59 at 20 μM in the WT IKs channel to Gmax = 1.08 ± 0.15 at 20 μM in the mutation (***p=0.0015) but does not change the V0.5 shift effect of Lin-tyr (Figure 5G and H).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from experimental data shown in Figure 5G and H.

claim: Aromatic PUFAs shift the voltage dependence and increase the current maximum by two independent mechanisms: one via interactions with S4 charges (R231) and one via interactions with K326.
source: Overall, Figure 5 demonstrates that aromatic PUFAs are shifting the voltage dependence and increasing the current maximum by two independent mechanisms: one via interactions with S4 charges (R231) and one via interactions with K326.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data showing independent effects of R231Q+Q234R and K326C mutations.

claim: Hydrogen bonding by the tyrosine's para-hydroxyl group is the reason for the large effect of PUFAs with tyrosine head groups on the IKs channel voltage-dependent activation.
source: Our experiments using fluorinated NALT (NAL-3F-tyr) to improve the hydrogen bonding capacity of the tyrosine head group demonstrated that hydrogen bonding by the tyrosine's para-hydroxyl group is the reason for the large effect of PUFAs with tyrosine head groups on the IKs channel voltage-dependent activation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data with 3F-NALT.

claim: S217A, Q220L, and S225A showed similar maximum shifts in voltage-dependent activation compared to the wild-type channel (WT + NALT: ΔV0.5 = –56.1 ± 3.6 mV; S217A + NALT: –65.9 ± 3.7 mV; Q220L + NALT: –59.5 ± 11.1 mV; S225A + NALT: –52.4 ± 3.7 mV at 20 μM).
source: We found that S217A, Q220L, and S225A showed similar maximum shifts in voltage-dependent activation compared to the wild-type channel (WT + NALT: ΔV0.5 = –56.1 ± 3.6 mV; S217A + NALT: –65.9 ± 3.7 mV; Q220L + NALT: –59.5 ± 11.1 mV; S225A + NALT: –52.4 ± 3.7 mV at 20 μM, ns; Figure 6C and D).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from experimental data shown in Figure 6C and D.

claim: The T224V mutation significantly attenuated the leftward shift in the voltage dependence of activation in response to NALT application from ΔV0.5 = –56.1 ± 3.6 mV in WT channels to ΔV0.5 = –32.1 ± 7.0 at 20 μM (p=0.03).
source: However, the T224V mutation significantly attenuated the leftward shift in the voltage dependence of activation in response to NALT application from ΔV0.5 = –56.1 ± 3.6 mV in WT channels to ΔV0.5 = –32.1 ± 7.0 at 20 μM (*p=0.03; Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: There was no difference in the voltage-shifting effects of NAL-phe between the T224V mutant and WT channels (WT + NAL-phe: ΔV0.5 = –12.5 ± 3.8 mV; T224V + NAL-phe: –13.2 ± 2.6 mV at 20 μM).
source: In contrast to the attenuation of the overall voltage shift observed when NALT was applied to the T224V, there was no difference in the voltage-shifting effects of NAL-phe between the T224V mutant and WT channels (WT + NAL-phe:ΔV0.5 = –12.5 ± 3.8 mV; T224V + NAL-phe: –13.2 ± 2.6 mV at 20 μM, ns; Figure 6F and G).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from experimental data shown in Figure 6F and G.

claim: The T224V mutation only reduces the efficacy of aromatic PUFAs that contain a hydrogen-bonding group like tyrosine.
source: These data demonstrate that the T224V mutation only reduces the efficacy of aromatic PUFAs that contain a hydrogen-bonding group like tyrosine.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data comparing NALT and NAL-phe effects on T224V mutant channels.

claim: T224 is a novel interaction site between the S3–S4 loop residue and hydrogen bonding moieties of aromatic PUFA head groups.
source: As a result, we have identified a novel interaction between the S3–S4 loop residue T224 and hydrogen bonding moieties of aromatic PUFA head groups.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data showing that T224V mutation specifically reduces NALT but not NAL-phe effects.

claim: The distance between the residues R231 and T224V in KCNQ1 is 9.1 Å.
source: Figure 7A shows the distance between the residues R231 and T224V in KCNQ1 is 9.1 Å
evidence: This is a measurement from structural data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The length of a tyrosine head group is 8.5 Å.
source: and the length of a tyrosine head group is 8.5 Å.
evidence: This is a measurement shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The tyrosine head group fits nicely in between R231 and T224 residues in silico, demonstrating the possibility of this interaction to occur.
source: The tyrosine head group fits nicely in between these two residues in silico, demonstrating the possibility of this interaction to occur (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from structural modeling shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Tyrosine PUFA analogues modulate the IKs channel via two independent interactions.
source: In our proposed mechanism, aromatic PUFA analogues modulate the IKs channel via two independent interactions (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data showing independent effects on voltage dependence and Gmax.

claim: In one site, the carboxyl group of aromatic PUFAs is interacting with R231 (in S4) and the distal –OH is hydrogen bonding with T224 (in the S3–S4 loop).
source: In one site, the carboxyl group is interacting with R231 (in S4) and the distal –OH is hydrogen bonding with T224 (in the S3–S4 loop) (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on experimental data from mutagenesis studies.

claim: In another site, the carboxyl group of aromatic PUFAs is interacting with K326 (in S6) and the distal electronegative atom stabilizes the PUFA via an electrostatic interaction.
source: In the other site, the carboxyl group is interacting with K326 (in S6) and the distal electronegative atom stabilizes the PUFA via an electrostatic interaction (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on experimental data from mutagenesis studies.

claim: Cation–pi interactions are not the primary mechanism through which tyrosine PUFAs activate the IKs channel.
source: Together, these data suggest that cation–pi interactions are not the primary mechanism through which these aromatic PUFA analogues activate the cardiac IKs channel.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data comparing tyrosine and phenylalanine PUFAs, and fluorinated phenylalanine PUFAs.

claim: Tri-fluorination of phenylalanine disperses the electrostatic surface potential that is necessary for cation–pi interactions.
source: Pless et al., 2014 demonstrated that tri-fluorination of phenylalanine disperses the electrostatic surface potential that is necessary for cation–pi interactions (Pless et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the effects of fluorination on cation-pi interactions, supported by a citation.

claim: 3,4,5F-NAL-phe is a more potent activator of the IKs channel compared to NAL-phe alone.
source: However, we find the opposite when we apply 3,4,5F-NAL-phe to the cardiac IKs channel, and see that 3,4,5F-NAL-phe is a more potent activator of the IKs channel compared to NAL-phe alone.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data comparing 3,4,5F-NAL-phe to NAL-phe.

claim: Aromatic PUFA analogues with highly electronegative atoms on the distal end of the aromatic head group have the most pronounced effects on the maximal conductance of the IKs channel.
source: These data suggest that aromatic PUFA analogues with highly electronegative atoms on the distal end of the aromatic head group have the most pronounced effects on the maximal conductance of the IKs channel.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data with brominated and fluorinated phenylalanine PUFAs.

claim: Brominated and fluorinated phenylalanine analogues fail to recapitulate the leftward ΔV0.5 observed with tyrosine PUFA analogues.
source: Although brominated and fluorinated phenylalanine analogues increase the maximal conductance of the IKs channel, these modified PUFAs still fail to recapitulate the leftward ΔV0.5 observed with tyrosine PUFA analogues.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data comparing brominated/fluorinated phenylalanine PUFAs to tyrosine PUFAs.

claim: Specific modifications to the aromatic PUFA head group can preferentially improve either the voltage-shifting or maximal conductance effects of PUFA analogues.
source: Most notably, these results suggest that specific modifications to the aromatic PUFA head group can preferentially improve either the voltage-shifting or maximal conductance effects of PUFA analogues.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data showing differential effects of various head group modifications.

claim: Adding highly electronegative groups to an aromatic ring, such as bromine and fluorine, most consistently improves the maximal conductance-increasing effects and reduces voltage dependence-shifting effects relative to PUFA analogues with a tyrosine or phenylalanine head group.
source: Our data suggests that adding highly electronegative groups to an aromatic ring, such as bromine and fluorine, most consistently improve the maximal conductance-increasing effects and reduce voltage dependence-shifting effects relative to PUFA analogues with a tyrosine or phenylalanine head group.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data with brominated and fluorinated phenylalanine PUFAs.

claim: Reducing the pKa of the –OH group (and increasing the potential for hydrogen bonding) preferentially improves the voltage-shifting effects on the IKs channel while leaving the effect on Gmax intact.
source: On the other hand, we found that reducing the pKa of the –OH group (and increasing the potential for hydrogen bonding), while leaving the effect on Gmax intact, preferentially improves the voltage-shifting effects on the IKs channel.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data with 3F-NALT.

claim: PUFA analogues have two independent effects on IKs channel activation.
source: Previous work has demonstrated that PUFA analogues have two independent effects on IKs channel activation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about PUFA mechanisms, based on previous work.

claim: PUFA analogues shift the voltage dependence of activation in the IKs channel through electrostatic effects on the channel voltage sensor.
source: PUFA analogues are known to shift the voltage dependence of activation in the IKs channel through electrostatic effects on the channel voltage sensor (Börjesson et al., 2008; Liin et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge about PUFA mechanisms, supported by citations.

claim: The voltage-shifting effect of PUFAs is mediated by interactions of the negative PUFA head group with the outermost positively charged arginine residues located in the S4 segment.
source: This is mediated by interactions of the negative PUFA head group with the outermost positively charged arginine residues located in the S4 segment (Liin et al., 2016; Liin et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge about PUFA mechanisms, supported by citations.

claim: A second effect of PUFAs on the IKs channel pore influences the maximal conductance of the IKs channel.
source: Recently, though, a second effect on the IKs channel pore has been reported to influence the maximal conductance of the IKs channel (Liin et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge about PUFA mechanisms, supported by a citation.

claim: The Gmax effect of PUFAs is mediated through electrostatic interactions between the PUFA head groups and K326 in the S6 segment.
source: This is mediated through electrostatic interactions between the PUFA head groups and a positively charged lysine residue in the S6 segment – K326 (Liin et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge about PUFA mechanisms, supported by a citation.

claim: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with the Kv7.1 (KCNQ1) channel identified two separate high-occupancy sites for linoleic acid: site 1 at R231 in the S4 segment, and site 2 at K326 in the S6 segment.
source: In addition, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with the Kv7.1 (KCNQ1) channel (the pore-forming domain for the IKs channel) (Yazdi et al., 2021) identified two separate high-occupancy sites for linoleic acid: site 1 at R231 in the S4 segment, and site 2 at K326 in the S6 segment (Yazdi et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge from MD simulations, supported by a citation.

claim: The more effective aromatic PUFAs act on sites at R231 in S4 and K326 in S6.
source: We here show that the more effective aromatic PUFAs also act on these sites in S4 and S6.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data with mutations at R231 and K326.

claim: The increased effects of the aromatic PUFAs, compared to non-aromatic PUFAs, are due to the additional hydrogen bonding in site 1 and electrostatic interactions in site 2 to better anchor them in these binding sites to increase their effects.
source: We therefore propose that the increased effects of the aromatic PUFAs, compared to non-aromatic PUFAs, are due to the additional hydrogen bonding in site 1 and electrostatic interactions in site 2 to better anchor them in these binding sites to increase their effects (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on experimental data.

claim: The aromatic rings of aromatic PUFAs have the potential to be modified to give preferential effects on either the IKs channel voltage sensor or channel pore.
source: As mentioned above, we also show that the aromatic rings have the potential to be modified to give preferential effects on either the IKs channel voltage sensor or channel pore.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data showing differential effects of various head group modifications.

claim: The hydrogen bonding capacity of the –OH on the tyrosine of NALT is necessary for it to have a more effective voltage dependence shift effect.
source: Our experiments with NAL-Phe and 3F-NALT show that the hydrogen bonding capacity of the –OH on the tyrosine of NALT is necessary for it to have a more effective voltage dependence shift effect.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data comparing NAL-Phe and 3F-NALT to NALT.

claim: The –OH group on the tyrosine of NALT hydrogen bonds with T224V, thereby improving the PUFA's ability to shift the voltage dependence.
source: This shows that the –OH group on the tyrosine of NALT hydrogen bonds with T224V, thereby improving the PUFA's ability to shift the voltage dependence.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data showing that T224V mutation reduces NALT effects.

claim: The hydrogen bond interaction between PUFAs and the 3–4 loop of the IKs channel is a novel mechanism to increase the effect of PUFAs to activate the IKs channel.
source: This hydrogen bond interaction between PUFAs and the 3–4 loop of the IKs channel is a novel mechanism to increase the effect of PUFAs to activate the IKs channel.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data identifying T224 as a hydrogen bonding partner.

claim: Drugs designed to target the hydrogen bond interaction with T224 would be more effective at shifting IKs channel voltage dependence.
source: These data suggest that the drugs designed to target this interaction would be more effective at shifting IKs channel voltage dependence.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about drug design based on the identified mechanism.

claim: Different aromatic PUFA analogues not only increase PUFA efficacy on activating the IKs channel, but their specific effects on IKs function can be modulated independently, either increasing the maximal conductance or voltage-shifting effect.
source: Overall, our findings suggest that different aromatic PUFA analogues not only increase PUFA efficacy on activating the IKs channel, but their specific effects on IKs function can be modulated independently, either increasing the maximal conductance or voltage-shifting effect.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data showing differential effects of various aromatic PUFA modifications.

claim: Patients with LQTS can have mutations in the IKs channel that cause either a decrease in Gmax or a rightward shift of voltage dependence.
source: Patients with LQTS can have mutations in the IKs channel that causes either a decrease in Gmax or a rightward shift of voltage dependence.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the heterogeneity of LQTS mutations.

claim: By independently modulating PUFAs to either increase Gmax or cause a leftward shift in voltage dependence, therapies may be designed that are more personalized to each patient's specific LQTS mutation.
source: By independently modulating PUFAs to either increase Gmax or cause a leftward shift in voltage dependence, we may be able to design therapies that are more personalized to each patient's specific LQTS mutation.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the therapeutic potential of the findings.

claim: The mechanistic understanding of how aromatic PUFAs have effects on the IKs channel may help to aid drug development for LQTS.
source: This novel mechanistic understanding of how aromatic PUFAs have these effects on the IKs channel may help to aid drug development for LQTS.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the translational potential of the findings.
